missing: This stage assesses trends and qualitative foil response. Acceptance requires the recorded C01 reference, a verified source, preserved physical settings, five complete cycles with repeatable cycles 2–5 and a healthy saved result.

The M10–M13 review was completed before C01. Expanded domains preserve the M13 cell-size controls and foil layers. PRE W04 must pass two consecutive 0.5% stability checks. The accepted reference policy is recorded with every run.
Q = mean wave Cx over cycles 2–5 (cycle 1 excluded) minus accepted C01 Cx. Negative Q indicates lower horizontal force. ΔFx is also reported in newtons.

Force–wave plots use one common foil reference at x = 0 m for existing and future runs. Older signals are extrapolated from the recorded upstream probe using measured wave propagation, with reconstruction details saved in the evidence. A direct measurement at x = 0 is preferred when available. Force timing is unchanged; lag calibration uses wave probes only.
Forcing and reflection quantification, time-step sensitivity, formal uncertainty and mass-flux closure are future studies; they do not block current acceptance or Q.

force_wave_comparison.phase_reference: sin(phi), a dimensionless harmonic phase guide; not a shared measured wave height
force_wave_comparison.force_normalization: Fixed accepted C01 subtracted; wave-cycle mean offsets retained
force_wave_comparison.caption: Phase-averaged foil response relative to accepted C01 (W01, W02, W03, W04, W04c, W04e, W04f, W04g, W04h, W04i, W04j, W05, W06, W07). Panels (a,c) show vertical and horizontal force differences in fixed domain axes from C01 versus wave phase at x = 0; panels (b,d) show the corresponding force–surface-elevation loops. Each curve is the mean of the complete response cycles 2–5, excluding cycle 1, after subtracting the same fixed C01 force from every sample. Horizontal zero lines denote C01. Wave-cycle mean force offsets are retained. C01 buoyancy-corrected vertical force is 1217.0568 N and horizontal force is 26.9981 N. Force differences are in newtons; surface elevations are measured from each cycle mean in metres, with no amplitude normalization. Phase zero is the upward crossing of the wave reference level at x = 0. The grey dashed sin(phi) curves are dimensionless phase guides; they do not represent one physical wave height shared by all cases. Loop coordinates use each case’s wave signal. Circles and squares mark the measured-wave crest and trough; arrows indicate increasing time. Where the direct x = 0 history is incomplete, the wave signal is propagated from upstream probes. Travel time is calibrated from a probe pair where available and otherwise estimated from wavelength and period. Forces are not shifted or fitted to the wave. These results describe trends in the selected quasi-2D M13 configuration.
